steps.name: Vanguard Operator
steps.text: This unripe texture, this slightly-too-salty flavor, oh, I'm finally home again!

steps.name: Logistics Operator
steps.text: It was just a long mission. You don't have to kiss the deck.

steps.name: Vanguard Operator
steps.text: Hey, you don't know how I take to Ursus food. It really doesn't agree with me.

steps.name: Vanguard Operator
steps.text: Our canteen's way better. I like everything here.

steps.name: Logistics Operator
steps.text: The way you just put it, it doesn't exactly sound like you like it.

steps.name: Vanguard Operator
steps.text: Something doesn't have to taste good for me to like it.

steps.name: Vanguard Operator
steps.text: I helped some survivors find their relatives and they thanked me with a banquet. A big, classy, noble shindig.

steps.name: Vanguard Operator
steps.text: But let's just say my palate isn't so refined.

steps.name: Logistics Operator
steps.text: Yeah, sure. You're totally dependent on the Rhodes Island Cafeteria.

steps.name: Logistics Operator
steps.text: So what was the mission?

steps.name: Vanguard Operator
steps.text: I'm pretty sure you know the deal. Resettling the refugees from Chernobog in other Ursus cities. Easy stuff, but time-consuming.

steps.name: Logistics Operator
steps.text: Forget I asked. I know how much refugee ops mean to you.

steps.name: Vanguard Operator
steps.text: Yeah. There's only so much we can do when there's so many of them and so few of us. But a life saved is a life saved.

steps.name: Vanguard Operator
steps.text: I heard Dobermann talking about how we're not in the best position with Ursus right now, so it's great that Amiya and the Doctor are still willing to do these rescue operations.

steps.name: Logistics Operator
steps.text: Sure. We lucked out with those two.

steps.name: Logistics Operator
steps.text: Well, there's another one we owe a lot of thanks too.

steps.name: Vanguard Operator
steps.text: Oh yeah, I heard about her out on the road. Some girl named Natalya?

steps.name: Logistics Operator
steps.text: Right. She's a big celebrity here now.
Oooh, my ears are burning.

steps.name: Logistics Operator
steps.text: Hey, Natalya, how you doing?

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Saren. And you are...?

steps.name: Vanguard Operator
steps.text: Codename Compass. Nice to meet you.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Compass.. a fine codename. Good afternoon. Would you mind if I joined you?

steps.name: Operator Saren
steps.text: By all means!

steps.name: Compass
steps.text: Hey, didn't I hear she was just a student?

steps.name: Compass
steps.text: This is no little girl! She's *gulp* pretty big!

steps.name: Operator Saren
steps.text: What do you think 'student' means?

steps.name: Compass
steps.text: I don't know how to talk to a lady like this!

steps.name: Operator Saren
steps.text: Relax. Natalya's real easy-going.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Did I happen to overhear that the good Compass has just returned from resettling refugees?

steps.name: Compass
steps.text: That's right. We were just talking about it.

steps.name: Operator Saren
steps.text: I was telling him all that you did to help.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Oh my role was completely trivial.

steps.name: Operator Saren
steps.text: You're too modest. If it wasn't for Natalya pushing the survivors along, we would've had a much tougher time.

steps.name: Compass
steps.text: The refugees were talking about her too. They said there was a kind young lady who told them Rhodes Island is good people.

steps.name: Compass
steps.text: And after hearing it right from Saren, I really gotta thank you, Miss Natalya.

steps.name: Compass
steps.text: The refugees having a good image of us makes all the difference in the world. Without you, I know things would've gone bad out there.

steps.name: Compass
steps.text: I mean, I was a refugee too. I know how they think. But it still sucks when you're trying to do good and people don't trust you.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: I did the absolute bare minimum. It was you out there doing the real work, Compass.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: And it's not that they don't trust Rhodes Island. It's that they've suffered a Catastrophe and they don't trust anyone.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: I sensed that Rhodes Island had everyone's best interests at heart. And having been Student Council President, I was used to this business. It's what I'm good at.

steps.name: Compass
steps.text: You hear that, Saren? This is how you talk to people. Listen up.

steps.name: Operator Saren
steps.text: Didn't I just say Natalya is easy-going?

steps.name: Operator Saren
steps.text: When word got around that the new kid was some aristocratic heiress, we were all worried about getting along.

steps.name: Operator Saren
steps.text: But it turns out she's good at her job, easy to talk to, super easy to get along with. We all love Natalya.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Oh my no. Everyone's only willing to put up with me because I'm so young.

steps.name: Compass
steps.text: Speaking of, did you decide to stay with Rhodes Island?

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: I did. I passed the Logistics Department's examination last week. I am now formally employed by Rhodes Island Pharmaceuticals.

steps.name: Compass
steps.text: Wow, that's great news. You're gonna love it here, trust me.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: I'm already very pleased.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: As long as we're on the subject, Mr. Saren, I've finished compiling the second refugee manifest, pairing names with destinations. If you wouldn't mind sending it along after lunch.

steps.name: Operator Saren
steps.text: What? Already?

steps.name: Operator Saren
steps.text: That means the refugees we saved all have somewhere to go?

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Yes. Aside from those who are still undergoing treatment.

steps.name: Operator Saren
steps.text: Incredible. It's a good thing the section chief put you on the task.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: I'm only doing my duty.

steps.name: Compass
steps.text: I guess I'd better go put in for the second resettlement op then.

steps.name: Operator Saren
steps.text: You want to head out there again? Didn't you just get done telling me you can't stand Ursus food?

steps.name: Compass
steps.text: Yeah, but seeing the survivors return to their homes and their relatives, seeing them so happy makes up for it.

steps.name: Compass
steps.text: Right, I'm about done with lunch. Help me with the tray, will you? I gotta go apply.

steps.name: Operator Saren
steps.text: Hey, bus your own tray!

steps.name: Operator Saren
steps.text: Sorry about him, Natalya. That's just how he is.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Our good Compass has quite the attachment to the refugees...?

steps.name: Operator Saren
steps.text: He does. You heard him say he was a refugee too, right? One of our teams saved him, so he's pretty gung ho about any ops that have to do with refugees.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: And you seem to get along well?

steps.name: Operator Saren
steps.text: Oh, yeah. I guess we do. He was in Logistics for a bit, before transferring to the front lines. We had some time together, our personalities clicked, and so we're friends.

steps.name: Operator Saren
steps.text: You're with that Ursus Student Self-government Group, right?

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Yes. But Son... Zima and the girls are front line operators like Compass, and I'm in Logistics.

steps.name: Operator Saren
steps.text: I heard you were all found together. You're very close too?

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: ...Yes, yes we are. We were together all that time. We're very close.

steps.name: Operator Saren
steps.text: You went through it as a group. That's good. Err, not to say that kind of hardship is good.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: I know what you mean.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Oh? Zima...

steps.name: Operator Saren
steps.text: Speak of the devil, huh?

steps.name: Operator Saren
steps.text: Is she staring at you?

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Forgive me, Saren. I must be going.

steps.name: Operator Saren
steps.text: Yeah, sure.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Are you looking for me, Zima?

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Are you okay? You look pale.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: I'm fine. I shouldn't have come looking for you. Forget I was here.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Hey, wait.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Don't touch me!

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Talk to me, Sonya. We haven't had a good talk since we came here.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Come to my room.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Have a seat. Care for a drink? Coffee? Tea? I have both.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: ...That's the aristocrat in you.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: You still have the strength to tease me. Looks like you're in better shape than I thought. Your face back there was a ghastly sight.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Let's call it coffee then. Rhodes Island has some fine beans, but I can't say the same for their tea.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: I've heard it has to do with the Chief Engineer. She's quite particular about her coffee. What do you think?

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: How should I know?

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Heh heh. I've been hearing nothing but praise lately. I'd missed your venomous tongue.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: And I'm sick of you already.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Do you take it with sugar?

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Really? It's black.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Alright.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Enjoy.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Bleh.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: It's too bitter, isn't it?

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Come now. Take a spoonful of sugar.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Did you drag me here to screw with me?

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: You're the one who wouldn't take the sugar, Sonya.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Hmph.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: And let's not forget, it was you who came looking for me.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: I already told you, that was a mistake. We're not friends. I don't like you.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: True. We're not friends. Nor is Anna my friend. We simply survived together.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Simply...

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Sonya, there are some things that are harder to say to those closest to you.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: If you were my friend, I would not have brought you here.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Some things can only be said to someone unimportant, someone who understands your situation.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: For me, the best person is Anna. But you'll do.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Mmm... Rosalind is too direct and open. While Lada is too honest and kindhearted. They won't do.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Surely you feel the same. Which means you have only me, I'm afraid. I'm honestly not surprised you came to me.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Does that mean you want to talk to me?

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Why?

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: ...Sonya, these last two months, how do you feel, fighting as an operator?

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: What do you mean 'feel?' It's just fighting. I guess it does suck to have to listen to that Doctor.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Your talking back to the Doctor even made it up to Logistics. You're quite something.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: ...I'm not like you. I don't talk fancy.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: What I really want to ask is, after all we've been through, do you not struggle to pick up a weapon?

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: ...I like fighting.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: I see... Still, I think it would be in your best interest to learn some 'fancy talk.' It could save your life.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: You don't have to worry.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: We may not be friends, but we've been through so much together. I think it's normal to care about you, as a colleague.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: And to tell the truth, I do quite like you. I would like to be your friend.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: ...Huh?

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: To be more precise, I'd say I envy you. Because you do so easily what I could never do.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Now then, Sonya, won't you tell me what made you seek me out?

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: ...I've been having nightmares lately.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Can you describe them to me?

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Alright. Let me guess. They must be something you can't talk to Anna about. Otherwise you wouldn't have come to me, right?

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: ...Right.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: I figured it out while we were still in Chernobog.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: You two have an understanding. You each know what the other needs, but you avoid talking about it.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: None of your business.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Relax, I'm not trying to tell you what to do. I'm in no position to be giving advice to others right now.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Let's talk about something else, Sonya. Do you plan to live your life as Zima now?

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: What do you mean?

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: I mean are you going to stay at Rhodes Island?

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: We don't have to. The people here are very understanding. If we wanted to leave, they would send us off somewhere peaceful.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: There are many survivors like us, rescued at the same time, already on their way back to Ursus.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: If we wanted to, we could go to another city in the Empire and start new lives.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: So why haven't you left?

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: I don't know.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Nice weather today. Isn't it, Sonya?

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Perfect for a picnics.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Hey.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Back when we were combing through the ruins, desperate for food, stretching a single bottle of water to last an entire day, I often thought to myself:

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: 'If I survive this, I'm going to find a lovely garden on a sunny afternoon and have a sumptuous picnic.'

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Hey!

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: But far more often I thought——

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: 'I wish you killed me that day.'

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Don't hesitate. Don't pity me. Don't think to save me. Look down at this wretched aristocrat girl, and swing your axe.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: It may have been the very best thing for me, had you just ended my life right there.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: There's still time.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: You really could?

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: We left that place, Sonya. We've returned to the civilized world.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: We must think as civilized people. We must use civilized methods to solve our problems. Those things that happened back there cannot happen again.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Who cares.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: You care. You're a good person, Sonya. 'General Zima,' Protector of the Weak, Bane of the Bullies.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Don't make me puke.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: That's the Sonya I heard rumors about.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: I just can't stand those punks who get a little bit of strength and think it's a license to bully.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: You must hate the aristocracy then?

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Duh. A bunch of a fake-ass self-important shitheads.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Yes. They, or rather, we are 'fake-ass self-important shitheads.'

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Since you brought me back, I don't think I've ever told you what happened to me before you showed up, did I?

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Nope. I just know you were in charge of that gang of nobles.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: I'll tell you the story sometime.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Whatever.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Most of the nobility and wealthy people fled the city when Reunion came, or even before.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: They know they were coming?

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Yes. They did.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: ...sons of bitches.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Indeed. But you know, nobles are selfish.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: You too?

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: So why did you stay?

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: My family was just too slow. We were trapped with some other noble families. Some houses didn't take the threat seriously, of course.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Oh.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Come now, don't give me that face. This background is important to frame the story. We'll get to the good part.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: In short, the students who were sent to your school fell into either the 'slow' or 'stupid' categories.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: We were at first meant to stay with our parents, for Reunion to use as hostages to bargain with the Empire. But in the end, we were separated and sent to the school.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: That's kinda weird.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: It was. Nobles make good hostages in a time of war. Not to be wasted.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: The aristocracy is elegant, noble, and should command respect. Even as a captive, one must never forget her house.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: You're all screwed in the head.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: The old me would have locked you in a two hour debate for saying that, Sonya. Because that's how I was raised.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: But now, I agree.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: There is no real difference between nobles and commoners. It's all window dressing. Scrape off the veneer and the aristocracy is truly ugly.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: We talked about how if it weren't for the first fire, if we didn't lose that food store, things wouldn't have gotten so bad.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: But Anna said even without the fire, something else would have happened.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: If I had been through that, I would have thought the same.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: But in any case, it's post-hoc—— 'What needed to happen to cause all that came after.'

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: The funny thing is, nobles don't need anything to happen. Put them together and they fight.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Why?

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Should I get into the differences between new and old nobility? The mayor's political leanings? How many factions there are in the Chernobog aristocracy?

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Could you, like, not do that?

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: But then you won't understand why they fight.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: I guess I'll just never understand.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: I'm not really interested in these things either. But as a daughter of the House of Rostov, I had to learn.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: All you need to know is that from the very first day we were locked up in the school, the noble students were backstabbing each other.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: I had no choice but to step forward as the Student Council President of #4 Secondary School and use my status to bring order.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: You mean you organized them to put an end to the infighting?

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Sounds reasonable, doesn't it? In order to stop my classmates from fighting, I stood up and took charge.

steps.name: Viktor
steps.text: Uh, ah...

steps.name: Nikola
steps.text: Don't think you rule the roost just because your father owns a mine, Pavel!

steps.name: Pavel
steps.text: A mere baron dares to take such a tone with me. He's lucky he doesn't find my blade in his chest.

steps.name: Pavel
steps.text: As for you, second son of the House of Ivanov, when did it become your turn to speak? Maybe you'd like a new hole in your torso as well?

steps.name: Nikola
steps.text: How dare you...?! My father is a councilor!

steps.name: Pavel
steps.text: A councilor? Do you know how many councilors come to my mother's soirees every Sunday?

steps.name: Pavel
steps.text: Oh, you don't? Because your father doesn't make the cut.

steps.name: Nikola
steps.text: You!

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Hold your tongue, Pavel!

steps.name: Pavel
steps.text: Please, Natalya, call me Pasha. You need not be so formal.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: I'm serious, Pavel Nikolaevich! You are not to start another senseless quarrel!

steps.name: Pavel
steps.text: As you wish, my esteemed President of the Student Council.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Tatyana, please bandage Viktor's wound.

steps.name: Tatyana
steps.text: O- of course!

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Ladies and gentlemen, we have been sealed inside this school. We know not what will happen. But I suspect that Reunion Movement won't let us go lightly.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Look at what you've become. It hasn't been twelve hours and you're arguing, fighting, even threatening to kill your fellow nobles.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Is this how the aristocracy behaves?!

steps.name: Anton
steps.text: Who the hell are you? Why should I listen to you?!

steps.name: Tatyana
steps.text: Because she is the president of the student council at #4 Secondary School, Natalya Andreyevna Rostova!

steps.name: Anton
steps.text: Y- you're the eldest daughter of Count Rostov?!

steps.name: Andrey
steps.text: She is the 'Pearl of #4,' the one whom Count Rostov has declared his heir.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: We have gathered here the nobility from each district secondary school. I do not wish to focus on my rank. I simply must impress upon you all the gravity of our situation.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: We find ourselves surrounded by many common students, and I do not want them to see such disgraceful conduct from us.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Furthermore, while we have been trapped here by the Reunion Movement, they will not seek to harm us, if they wish to secure concessions from the Empire.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Are we going to waste our precious lives on such infighting?!

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: We need unity, now more than ever!

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Of course, we now know Reunion didn't give a damn about us aristocrats.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Anyway, I was able to put a stop to their fighting. But in a situation like that, pretty words and a fancy title will only get you so far.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Sonya, do you know why the Empire of Ursus is as strong as it is?

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: In fact, there were quite a few noble students who were unwilling to submit to my authority, or share the same room with someone else, and left the group.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: In the end, I had some three dozen under me.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: At the time, I thought I had done very well.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: So that's why there were still so many noble shitstains lurking around.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Yes, I'm sure they made their own groups as well.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: How was I supposed to know?

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: It's a shame. I'm enjoying this conversation with you, but I do wish Anna was here for it.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Don't change the subject.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Oh, I'm sorry. I do have more to say, but it's hard to get the words out.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Ursus is what it is today because of war. The previous monarch waged endless war, pillaging resources, and investing them in the next campaign.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: As long as there was war, the Empire could function, the people united in their common struggle.

steps.name: Nikola
steps.text: I... I agree with President Rostova.

steps.name: Pavel
steps.text: I will submit to the President's leadership.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: If you are all willing to put your trust in me, I am willing to serve the group.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: (I was able to stop the fight, barely, but what do I do next...?)

steps.name: Pavel
steps.text: That being the case, I have a proposal.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Oh?

steps.name: Pavel
steps.text: You were correct when you said we have a responsibility to preserve the dignity of the aristocracy.

steps.name: Pavel
steps.text: Therefore, it's time the commoners offered us a contribution, to ensure we can live in such dignity.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: You mean...?

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Yes, I agreed to let them prey on the commoners.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Sonya, I used to think myself a good person.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: At least, at the time, that's how I thought.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: I would find the social machinations of the aristocracy boring and hypocritical, I would bemoan the tragedies of the world, I would even serve meals to refugees.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: But I will not lie to you, or to myself.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: At that time, to unite the nobles, I allowed them to pillage.
'Wham!' The white-haired girl is thrown to the floor. She takes a few solid hits to the face. And as the slight trickle of crimson blood slips from her mouth, it curls into a smile.
A tragic smile.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: *Cough,* *cough...*

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: You piece of...

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: I am a monster.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: But you know, Sonya, I wouldn't realize it if I never spent that time with you, if I never came to Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Without these experiences, I would not think as I do now.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: You taught me that I am not noble, in the true sense of the word. And that is the most painful knowledge I must endure.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: That is why I say it would have been better had you killed me like you did my companions.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: I could have died peacefully, indulging in the fantasy that I was a good girl, that I was forced by circumstance to do what I did.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: ...Do you know, Sonya, what this is?

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: A letter opener.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: These past few months, I have twenty-six times thought to slit my wrists. Fifteen times I thought to slash open my throat.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: ...You can count 'em, huh?

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Because each time I fail, I laugh at myself for being such a stupid coward. That stays with me.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Of course, I've considered more aristocratic methods as well: poisoned tea, a saber. I've even thought carefully about what calligraphic style to use in my suicide note.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Unfortunately, all of those methods would be discovered before I could pull off the deed. And I don't want to make trouble.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: What's your point?

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: I told Rhodes Island: I want to stay here and do what I can for the people of Ursus.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: I told myself: Natalya, this is your atonement.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: But is that true?

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Whenever I think of Nikola's smile, of any of their faces as they came to me, triumphant after robbing the commoners; of my cowardice as I smiled back at them, rather than reprimanding their evil.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Whenever I think of all that I let them do, of the plans I would make for them, of the joy I took in our comfortable hoard of supplies.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Whenever I think of all the screaming and crying I ignored, of how I thought myself innocent by way of circumstance, of how I began to grow accustomed to living that way.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Sonya, can you believe it? That in that entire battle royale, I did not kill a single person?

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: And yet, I bear the most guilt.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Did you think I brought you here to tell you what you should do?

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: No, Sonya. I don't know. I have no idea. About anything.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: I don't even know how to tell people I don't know! All I can do is put on that stupid facade that I have everything perfectly under control as I drag you in here!

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Do you...?

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Phew, I'm sorry. I lost my composure.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: ...Do you want something to drink?

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Black tea, please. Thank you.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Okay.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: So uh, where do you keep the black tea?

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: You've got a shitload of different tea boxes over here. I can't tell what's what.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Oof.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Hup.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: I'll get it, Sonya.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Uh, sorry.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: It just occurred to me you probably don't know how to make tea. Forgive the momentary lapse in judgment that pushed you to do something you're not good at.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Why you...

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Say, Sonya, what exactly were you thinking back then?

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: After the fire, I ran as fast as I could only to be caught by some other students. Why did you save me?

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: You knew of course that I was the leader of the nobles wreaking havoc just days before.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: I forget.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: You probably just looked too pathetic.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Then why would you let me join the Self-Governing Group?

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Because Anna said it was okay.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Do you want me to hate you, Natalya?

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: I don't know. Can you hate me?

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: I've never seen a shithead admit she's a shithead before.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: So a shithead who admits she's a shithead isn't a shithead anymore?

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: ...Do you want me to crush you?

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: I'm no masochist. It's just, how should I say? I'd like to be honest with you, um, after all that you just heard, to avoid any misunderstandings.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Maso... what?

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Oh, that's just a kind of 'hobby' popular in aristocratic circles. I've only heard rumors, actually. Don't worry about it.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: As long as I don't have to kick your ass again.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: You don't want to?

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Do you prefer Columbian or Victorian? Tea, that is.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: ...You're right back to your old self.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Whatever, I can't drink it anyway.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: It's how I was raised. I must show my most refined side at all times.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Sugar?

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: ...Yeah.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Sorry, you can't sweeten this kind of tea. Drink it straight, please.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: You suck.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Hmph.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Look, Natalya, I don't know how I'm supposed to cheer you up. And anyway I really don't wanna.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Oh? Not only do you not hate me, you want to comfort me?

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Shut your tea hole.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Alright, alright.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: I hate trying to comfort people. Every time I try, I screw everything up.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: All I can do is tell you what I'm thinking.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: You asked me a minute ago if I was gonna keep on living as Zima.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: The answer is yes.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: My mom and dad died in Chernobog. There's nothing for me to go back to. I don't wanna go back to Ursus. So that's that.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: I think I should be able to understand your pain or whatever, but I really don't.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: At first, I thought you wanted to justify yourself. Punks talk like that when they want to sucker-punch me while I'm distracted. But you seem legit sad. Why?

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Those noble shitstains wouldn't have been any better off without you. And you're not the one who turned them into dickheads anyway. You didn't make all that happen.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: It was actually me...

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: You?

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Nothing, forget it. But if I was one of those nobles, I might've liked having a leader like you. Same way Istina chose me.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: You did what you could.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: I only hate you because you were my enemy before you weren't. Also I hate nobles. That's all.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Oh, and I have nightmares, and the nightmares make me puke, and then I can't sleep because I'm sad.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: But doing what you can to survive isn't bad.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: And I don't think it was bad to let you live.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: You think you're a shithead. But I know, without you, just relying on Anna, we never would've survived those next couple weeks.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Just go for a run. Eat when you're hungry. Sleep when you're tired. Better than sitting around moping.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Hup.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Ahahahahaha.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: What's making you laugh like that? Jeez, you're tearing up.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Nothing. It's just, this is why it's nice to chat with you.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: If it were Anna and me, we'd be bawling our eyes out over each other by now.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: She doesn't like you either, don't forget.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: I know. Pfft. Hahaha! I know.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Listen, Sonya.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: What are you doing?

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: I want you to know, you completely failed to address my problem.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: I'm way too lazy to care.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: And I think there's nothing I could do to help with yours.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: But you were right on one point: we survived.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Do you think we'll get over it, in the end?

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: The circle beneath our feet, the night, the maze, our minds, our thoughts, the abyss.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Could you use like, real words?

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Right, right. Anyway, operators all have codenames, right? If I were to become an operator, what should my codename be?

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: How should I know? Anna picked mine.

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Okay. What do you think of Rosa?

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Ursine for 'dew?'

steps.name: Natalya
steps.text: Yes, like morning dew. Can you call me 'Rosa?'

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: O...kay?

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: It's settled. If I'm to become an operator, they'll call me Rosa.
